PERMITS AND LICENSES COMMITTEE
  MINUTES
  August 8, 2019

A meeting of the Permits and License Committee was held on Thursday, August 8, 2019,
at 2:09 pm in the Community Room A, 1st Floor.

Roll Call:  Members Present:  Harjinder Singh, Administration
  Cheryl Moore, City Clerk’s
  Lt. David Salcedo, Police Department
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Planning & Building Department

  Staff Present:  Peggy L. Velasquez, Finance Department

Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items
During public comments any person may address the Permits & License Committee,
provided the item is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Permits & License
Committee.
Chairman Singh asked if there were any persons present who wished to address the
Permits & License Committee on any item on the Agenda.
Chairman Singh reported that there were no public requests to speak.

Agenda Items

A motion was moved and seconded to approve the minutes from the meeting held on July
25, 2019 and Special Meeting of June 27, 2019.

Permit Request (s):

Item #1:  Shelli Boone of Willie Agee Playhouse and the City of Inglewood to host a
  3rd Anniversary Celebration at the Willie Agee Playhouse at Edward
  Vincent Jr. Park, on Saturday, August 17, 2019, from 10:00 a.m. – 6:00
  p.m.; required staffing 1 Sgt., 2 Police Officers, 2 Patrol Cars, to be parked
  in designated areas for high visibility from 9am-7pm; provide Inglewood
  Police Department a list of venders, artists, performers, dignitaries and
  presenters no later than 7 days prior to event; no drones without
  appropriate required approval; Not Alcohol or Smoking or consumption of
  Cannabis products, cigarettes, cigars and vapers; Park Staffing for crowd
  management, Adhere to all applicable Inglewood Municipal Code rules and
  regulations, including noise and signage, local, state and federal laws.
  Motion carried unanimously. (Activity No. 00276318)

Item #2:  Fr. John Botros of Holy Annunciation Church to host a Holy Virgin Mary
  Festival at 2225 W. Manchester, on August 23, 2019, from 4:00 p.m. -
  10:00 p.m.; August 24, 2019, from 9:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. and August 25,
  2019, from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.; Father Botros advised the Committee
  that the event would no longer be on the parking lot but inside the church
  common area, Police therefore recommended the deployment of 2-4
 Permits & License Committee  August 8, 2019

  church staff for crowd management; anyone directing traffic in parking lot
  shall wear reflective vest(s) to manage the parking lot for people attending
  the event;. Adhere to all applicable Inglewood Municipal Code rules and
  regulations, including noise and signage, local, state and federal laws.
  Motion carried unanimously. (Activity No. 00276132)

Item #3:  Laura Santo of Turner AECOM Hunt JV to host a Celebratory Event – 10
  Million Trade Hours Worked at 1000 S. Prairie Avenue, on August 28,
  2019, from 10:45 a.m. - 1:00 p.m., provide adequate security to maintain
  and monitor crowd control; Any person directing traffic is required to wear
  highly-visible retro-reflective vests; IPD to provide extra patrol as time
  permits, Watch Commander will be notified; Maintain site at all times,
  ensuring site is properly cleaned immediately at the end of the event;
  Ensure safe pedestrian and vehicular circulation on/off site; and Adhere to
  all applicable Inglewood Municipal Code rules and regulations, including
  noise and signage, local, state and federal laws. Motion carried
  unanimously. (Activity No. 00276241)

Item #4:  Brett Fernau of Inglewood Church of Scientology to host a Unity on Market
  Street Block Party at 315 Market Street, on August 31, 2019, from 12:00
  p.m. - 7:00 p.m. was held over to August 22, 2019 (Activity No. 00276237)

Lt. David Salcedo, Inglewood Police Department:
submitted Standard Recommendations for all approved Tobacco Retailers License:

1.  Must adhere to all City of Inglewood Municipal Codes (IMC), specifically; CHAPTER 8:
  Article 8. REGULATIONS FOR BUSINESSES ENGAGED IN THE SALE OF TOBACCO
  PRODUCTS;
2.  Must adhere to all State and Federal Rules and Regulations;
3.  Sales or display of single cigarettes is strictly prohibited;
4.  Sales of tobacco, hookah, vapor and e-cigarette products to minors, under age 21 is strictly
  prohibited;
5.  Persons purchasing tobacco or any related tobacco products shall have a valid government-
  issued identification on their person at all times to enforce laws restricting underage access
  to tobacco use, including hookah products;
6.  Sales or display of any type of weapons, i.e., clubs, swords, knives, pepper spray, Taser/Stun
  guns is strictly prohibited;
7.  Tobacco Retailer business owners and/or new applicants or their designees are subject to
  random Permits & Licenses establishment inspections at any time of the day or night by any
  Police or Code Enforcement Officers, purpose of random inspections is to enforce business
  establishments to adhere to the regulations set forth by the City of Inglewood for Community
  Public Health & Safety;
8.  California State Board of Equalization Tobacco Retailers license must be current;
9.  Approval for retail sales of tobacco products within existing business ONLY;
10.  NO sales of tobacco (including vaporized / hookah products) to minors / underage persons.
  All persons purchasing tobacco or any related tobacco products SHALL have valid ID on
  their person at all times to ensure the restriction of underage tobacco use, including hookah
  products;
11.  Submit all state tobacco renewal certificates if applicable;
12.  NO loitering of persons outside of the location;

13.  NO LOITERING / PANHANDLING SIGNS MUST BE POSTED and visible to outside of the
  business. Proof of signage posted by applicant shall be submitted to finance (i.e. photo of
  signage);
14.  The following is not allowed: the use of or illegal sales or cultivation of marijuana/cannabis
  products, any regulated cannabis products, any use or possession of illegal or unauthorized
  narcotics, narcotic paraphernalia per H&S11364.5 - i.e.; any pipes specifically used to ingest
  illegal narcotics, this would also include glass cylindrical, tube or bubble shaped pipes used
  specifically to smoke / ingest illegal narcotics. Sales of Tobacco pipes are acceptable;
  Applicant and employees are expected to be active participants in calling/notifying police for
  police related, unusual, illegal, and/or activity that may necessitate a police response or
  response from other city government services (i.e. Code Enforcement, Planning, Finance,
  Public Works, Fire Dept., Etc.);
15.  Applicant and employees are expected to be active participants in calling/notifying police for
  police related, unusual, illegal, and/or activity that may necessitate a police response or
  response from other city government services (i.e. Code Enforcement, Planning, Finance,
  Public Works, Fire Dept., Etc.); and
16.  The following is not allowed inside the business without proper authorization via the P&L
  Committee review and permit: PARTIES, SOCIAL EVENTS OR GATHERINGS OF
  ANYKIND, MUSIC BOXES (juke box), NO LIVE BANDS / MUSIC, DISC JOCKIES (DJ'S)
  PERFORMANCE, DANCE HALL, ETC. APPLICANT MUST HAVE REASONABLE
  BUSINESS HOURS (TIME OF DAY OR NIGHT) OF OPERATION.

Public Comments
Chairman Singh asked if there were any persons present who wished to address the
Permits & License Committee on any matters connected with items on the Agenda.
Chairman Singh reported that there were no public requests to speak.

There being no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 2:59 p.m.

  Respectfully submitted,
  Peggy L. Velasquez, Recording Secretary
